advice: Propose one-entry reuse of the existing panel32 assembly helper. In the helper body, keep the ABI prologue, one `smstart`, one 64 KiB scratch allocation, one `smstop`, and epilogue. Add an outer 16-panel loop around the existing pack block (`Lpanel32_70`) and 16-column tile block (`Lpanel32_330`). Preserve the original B, A, and C bases in audited callee-saved registers. For panel p=0..15, set A to A_base+p*65536 and C to C_base+p*65536; reset B to B_base and the pack cursor to the scratch base. Keep the current FP32 K loop, ZA setup and stores unchanged. Reset SP to the allocated scratch base after packing and restore it only after the last panel. This tests whether replacing sixteen helper calls and streaming-region transitions with one entry/exit improves the complete n=512 call. All packing, computation, and transitions stay timed. The supplied feasibility review supports the mapping, but this is advice, not a measured fact or a selected experiment.
risks: This assembly rewrite has register-preservation, stack-lifetime, pointer-reset, and SME-state risks. Keep stack alignment and callee-saved registers valid; do not add C calls inside the streaming region. Confirm every output row is written once, beta-zero behavior is retained, scratch remains allocated while consumed, and the complete LIBXSMM BSD notice remains. Do not claim that fewer transitions cause a gain without paired measurements.
